subject: Intermittent p95/p99 spikes on long-window (32k) requests - customer impact
messages:
From: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@starlithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:13:00Z
Subject: High p99 latency for 32k requests - batch jobs failing

Vanessa —

We started seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency late yesterday night across a subset of our inference batches that upload ~30–32k token contexts. The p95 is up from ~420ms to ~1.9s and p99 has spiked to 9–12s intermittently. This is impacting our overnight reconciliation jobs — a handful of retries have timed out and downstream pipelines are backing up.

Attached is a screenshot of the Datadog alert and a CSV with request IDs for the failures. Sample request id: req_20261118_4f7b. We haven't changed our client code. Can you triage urgently and advise a mitigation?

Elaine
Ops Lead, Starlit Health
Attachment: p99_spike_screenshot.png (image)
Attachment: p95_p99_trends_11_18_11_20.csv (csv)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@starlithealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: High p99 latency for 32k requests - batch jobs failing

Hi Elaine — thanks for the alert and the data. We’re triaging now. A few quick asks while we investigate:

- Can you share 1–2 full request payloads (redact PHI if present) or the exact sequence-length distribution for the failing jobs?
- Are these jobs hitting the Hosted API (api.redwood.com) or your Dedicated endpoint?

Immediate actions we’ll take: Rishi will scan serving traces for queueing/KV-cache behavior and check autoscaler events. Marissa will start an incident channel and coordinate communications. If needed, we can temporarily route your 32k requests to a reduced-context fallback (16k) to ease pressure while we fix the root cause — want to confirm whether you can accept a short-term truncation.

We’ll update in the next 30–60 minutes.

—Vanessa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@starlithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: High p99 latency for 32k requests - initial triage

Elaine / team — quick triage update: we’ve pulled traces for req_20261118_4f7b and related IDs. Preliminary findings:

- Symptoms line up with rapid KV cache growth per connection for long-context sessions; large prefix KVs are causing memory working-set churn and occasional GC/eviction storms on a subset of hosts.
- Autoscaler reacted to CPU/memory pressure and cycled pods; the pod warmup + cache rehydration caused request queuing for tens of seconds, explaining the 9–12s p99 spikes.
- Error rates are slightly elevated (HTTP 5xxs ~0.6% on affected routes) during spike windows.

Temporary mitigations I can apply now (requires customer sign-off):
1) Emergency request-length clamp: silently truncate any context > 16k tokens for affected routes (non-destructive) — should drop p99 significantly.
2) Enable conservative prefix-KV eviction policy (reduces cache churn, may slightly increase token compute).
3) Route a fraction (10–20%) of traffic to a dedicated capacity pool if you have Dedicated enabled; otherwise we can spin a short-lived higher-memory pool.

I’m attaching the p95/p99 export and a small patch for the eviction policy. If you approve option (1) we’ll deploy within 20 minutes and monitor.

—Rishi
Serving Infra Engineer
Attachment: incident_playbook_patch.diff (text)
Attachment: p95_p99_trends_11_18_11_20.csv (csv)
From: Ken Park <ken.park@starlithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@starlithealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: High p99 latency for 32k requests - approval to throttle to 16k

Vanessa / Rishi — thanks for the quick triage. We can tolerate a short-term clamp to 16k for the overnight reconciliation runs — better to succeed than to have repeated timeouts. Please proceed with the silent truncation and let us know the rollback plan. Also, please outline expected functional impact (are any model outputs likely to be truncated meaningfully?).

—Ken
Senior SRE, Starlit Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:02:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Starlit Health p99 regression — exec awareness and credit request

Neha — looping you in for awareness and decisioning. Starlit (strategic customer, ARR ~$420k) is experiencing p99 spikes on long-window (32k) hosted API requests; they approved a temporary clamp to 16k to stop failures.

Impact summary:
- Time window: 2026-11-18 02:00–06:00 UTC (observed spikes)
- Peak p99: 9–12s on affected routes; baseline ~0.45s
- Error rate: 0.6% 5xx during spikes
- Customer impact: delayed overnight batch runs, manual retries, internal incidents at Starlit

Asks:
1) Approve offering one month of service credit for the incident (we’ve had past credits for SLA issues).
2) Approve prioritizing a targeted Dedicated capacity quote for Starlit (by EOD tomorrow) and prioritize the engineering fix to avoid future autoscaler churn.

We’ve applied the emergency clamp (16k) with Rishi; monitoring is in progress.

—Vanessa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Starlit Health p99 regression — exec awareness and credit request

Thanks for the heads up — please proceed.

- Approve the one-month service credit to Starlit Health.
- Prioritize the engineering mitigation to stabilize KV eviction/autoscaler interaction. Rishi: please add an item to the SRE sprint and tag INF-5421.
- Marissa: work with Vanessa to prepare a Dedicated capacity quote and the handoff doc.

Please keep me posted; I want a postmortem within 72 hours that includes root cause, timeline, and action owners.

—Neha
VP, Product & GTM
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@starlithealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T17:45:00Z
Subject: Incident update: clamp applied, p99 improved, next steps

Elaine / Ken — final update for the incident window: 

Actions taken:
- 2026-11-18 11:25 UTC: emergency silent clamp to 16k tokens applied to affected hosted routes.
- 2026-11-19 02:12 UTC: conservative prefix-KV eviction enabled on the pool serving Starlit traffic.
- 2026-11-19 22:30 UTC: routed 15% of traffic to temporary higher-memory pool while we rebuild cache warmup heuristics.

Observed outcome (post-mitigation):
- p95 returned near baseline (~0.5s); p99 reduced to ~1.3–1.8s in peak windows.
- 5xx error spikes subsided to <0.1%.

Next steps:
- Rishi / Infra: schedule the KV eviction/autoscaler fix and include INF-5421 in next SRE sprint.
- Marissa / AE: Dedicated capacity quote and handoff by EOD 2026-11-21.
- Postmortem: scheduled; delivery within 72 hours (will include timeline, root cause, remediation plan, and opportunities for improved long-window handling).

Attachments: p95_p99_trends_11_18_11_20.csv, incident_playbook_patch.diff

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with the postmortem.

—Vanessa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
